name: Mobb Deep
sources: HipHopDX — Havoc on his production roots / Infamous kit
notes: Queensbridge dread-minimalism, and the two parameters that make it are dissonance and absence. The motifs are two-note tritone-adjacent figures rather than chords, so `halfStepDissonance` is the highest on this axis by a wide margin and `maxChords` is the lowest. The hats are not continuous — often only the offbeats — which is the one place a boom-bap kit is allowed to stop. Melody sits high-mid on purpose so the sustained sub can own everything below it. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick`, not a held note, and that is a limit of this model's own harmony rather than a reading of the record.** The research says a near-DC sine sustained on the tonic with no melodic movement. `reese_sustain` is the only rhythm that holds a note. ⛔ **TASK-162 fixed the engine half and it was NOT enough here, which is worth knowing before anyone tries again.** `grid::phrase_spans` now re-articulates a held span every phrase, so `reese_sustain` no longer emits one note per chord — but this model authors a single static `i`, so every span lands on the same pitch and it still measured under the 500-distinct floor when switched over on 2026-08-13. Re-articulation cannot manufacture variety out of one chord and one pitch, and inventing movement the records do not have would be the dishonest fix. `mirror_kick` over a kick that only plays 1 and 3& is the nearest honest thing: two low roots a bar, which reads as sustained at this tempo. `followRootsProb` keeps it on the tonic. ⛔ `chords.impliedByRiff` is set, and it is a description rather than an exemption. The research: *"2-bar loops built from a single sampled or played piano/vibe figure; i (static)"*. One chord is the part. ⚠ `phraseBars` reaches 4 as well as 2 — weighted 4:1 so the 2-bar loop the research describes still dominates. At 2 bars alone the counter saturated at 0.93 of the 0.98 floor: shape length is what a counter's variety is combinatorial in, and one length is one shape. ⚠ `snareRoll.pitchWalk` is inherited rather than authored: the research says nothing about how these producers pitch a roll, and lowering it was an invention that `drum_pitch.rs` correctly refused — a roll owes a producer three pitches unless the style is a train beat. ⚠ `hihat.continuous` is false — the research says the hats are often only on the offbeats, and this is the one boom-bap kit allowed to stop. `fillDensity` is 0.3 rather than the 0.1 first authored because at 0.1 some seeds produced a bar with no hats at all, which `drums_hats.rs` refuses: a model that declares a hat block owes every seed a hat. ⚠ `chordDurationBeats` carries this model's chord variety rather than more progressions. Its harmony is one or two chords by description, and `melodic_variety.rs` still requires the generated chord part to reach 55 distinct outputs — so what varies is how long the loop sits on a chord, not what the chord is. Adding families it does not play would have been the dishonest fix. ⚠ The i–VII family is INFERRED, not researched — the research names only the static form. It carries a low weight and exists because the generated chord part still owes a producer 55 distinct outputs over 200 seeds; it is the first thing to delete if this model ever sounds busier than the records do. ⚠ **`drums.kick.lockTo808` removed (2026-08-17, 808 gate).** This kit has no 808 — `bass808` is `null` here or in the parent it inherits — and `lockTo808` is the one parameter that says *how much of the kick the 808 follows*, so in this file it described a pairing that does not exist: `generators::drums::bass808` returns on `block.is_none()` before the value is ever read, which makes it provably dead here. Where it was NOT dead was in the artists and producers who extend this kit and author an 808 of their own: they inherited the zero, `kicks.iter().filter(|_| rng.random_bool(0.0))` kept nothing, and their sub lane was silent at every seed — `bass808::every_shipped_model_with_an_808_produces_a_playable_line` reported "no 808 at all" for 35 of them. Removing it restores the engine's documented default of 1.0 for exactly those children and changes nothing here. ⚠ No researched claim moved: this kit's own statement about the 808 is the `bass808: null` beside it, and that is untouched.
